exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Choosing a Mystery
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lin: Mr Brown asked us to choose a famous mystery for our class project. Any ideas?
Kate: How about Stonehenge? No one is sure why those huge stones were put up.
Lin: That's interesting, but lots of groups will pick it. Let's choose something different.
Kate: Then what about the giant statues on Easter Island?
Lin: I like that. We could find out how such heavy statues were moved with simple tools.
Kate: Good. I'll search for some theories online, and you can prepare the questions for our survey.
Lin: Perfect. Let's meet in the library on Friday to put it all together.
Kate: See you then. This is going to be fun.
exercises.translation_cn: 林说 Brown 老师让他们为班级课题选一个著名谜团;Kate 提议巨石阵,但林觉得太多组会选,想换一个;Kate 改提复活节岛石像;林赞同,想研究岛民如何用简单工具搬动沉重石像;Kate 负责上网找理论,林准备调查问题;两人约周五在图书馆汇总。

questions.stem: What does Mr Brown want the students to do?
options: Choose a famous mystery for a project.

options: Because it is too far to reach.
Because many other groups will pick it.
Because it is not mysterious at all.

questions.stem: Which mystery do they finally choose?
options: The giant statues on Easter Island.

questions.stem: What will Kate do for the project?
options: Build a model of the statues.

questions.stem: When and where will the two students meet?

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 Born to Explore
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: People have always wanted to explore the world around them.
Long ago, our ancestors climbed mountains and crossed wide seas.
They simply wanted to see what lay beyond the next hill.
Today we send probes far into space to study other worlds.
As long as something is unknown, someone will want to discover it.
exercises.translation_cn: 人们一直想探索周遭的世界;很久以前,我们的祖先翻山越海;只是想看看下一座山那边有什么;今天我们把探测器送往遥远的太空去研究其他星球;只要还有未知,就总会有人想去发现。

questions.stem: What have people always wanted to do?
What did our ancestors do long ago?
Why did they want to cross the next hill?
options: To see what lay beyond it.

questions.stem: What do we send far into space today?
When will someone want to discover something?
options: As long as it stays unknown.

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 At the Science Museum
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Guide: Welcome. This model shows China's Chang'e-4 probe.
Tom: Is that the one that landed on the far side of the moon?
Guide: Yes. It was the first probe ever to land softly there, back in 2019.
Tom: Why is the far side so hard to reach?
Guide: We can never see it from Earth, and radio signals cannot reach it directly.
Tom: So how did people on Earth talk to the probe?
Guide: Engineers sent up a special satellite to pass messages back and forth.
Tom: That's clever. I'd love to work on a mission like this one day.
exercises.translation_cn: 讲解员欢迎参观,介绍这是中国嫦娥四号探测器的模型;Tom 问是不是降落在月球远端的那台;讲解员说是,2019年它是首个在那里软着陆的探测器;Tom 问为何远端难以到达;因为从地球永远看不到它、无线电信号也无法直接到达;工程师便发射了一颗专门的卫星来回传递信息;Tom 说很巧妙,希望有朝一日能参与这样的任务。

questions.stem: What does the museum model show?
When did the probe land on the far side?
Why is the far side of the moon hard to reach?
options: It is covered in deep water.
It is far too bright to land on.
Radio signals cannot reach it directly from Earth.
It is always crowded with people.

questions.stem: How did engineers talk to the probe?
options: They could not talk to it at all.

questions.stem: What does Tom hope to do one day?
options: Work on a mission like this one.
Move to the moon at once.

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 Facts about the Deep Ocean
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: The deep ocean is one of the least explored places on Earth.
At the bottom of the deepest trench, the water is freezing and dark.
The pressure there could easily crush an ordinary submarine.
Even so, scientists have found strange fish living in the deep.
Each new dive teaches us a little more about this hidden world.
exercises.translation_cn: 深海是地球上探索最少的地方之一;在最深海沟的底部,海水冰冷而漆黑;那里的压力能轻易压垮一艘普通潜艇;尽管如此,科学家仍在深处发现了奇怪的鱼;每一次新的下潜都让我们对这个隐秘世界多了解一点。

questions.stem: How well explored is the deep ocean?
options: It is one of the least explored places.
It is a popular holiday spot.
It is very easy to reach.

questions.stem: What is the water like at the bottom of the trench?
What could the pressure do to an ordinary submarine?
What have scientists found in the deep?
What does each new dive do?
options: Teaches us more about this hidden world.

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 A Nessie Documentary
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Sam: I watched a documentary about the Loch Ness Monster last night.
Mia: Oh, Nessie! Did they finally prove it is real?
Sam: No. They showed many old photos, but none of them was clear.
Mia: I thought scientists searched the lake with modern machines.
Sam: They did, but the machines found nothing unusual at all.
Mia: So why do people still visit the lake every year?
Sam: I suppose they just enjoy the mystery and hope to see something.
Mia: Maybe one day someone will get a clear photo. Who knows?
exercises.translation_cn: Sam 说昨晚看了一部关于尼斯湖水怪的纪录片;Mia 问是否终于证明它是真的;Sam 说没有,片中展示了许多旧照片,但都不清晰;Mia 以为科学家用现代仪器搜过湖;Sam 说搜过,但仪器什么异常都没发现;Mia 问那为何人们每年还去;Sam 觉得他们只是享受这份神秘、盼着看到点什么;Mia 说也许哪天有人能拍到清晰照片,谁知道呢。

questions.stem: What did Sam watch last night?
options: A documentary about the Loch Ness Monster.

questions.stem: Did the documentary prove Nessie is real?
options: No, the photos were not clear.

questions.stem: What did the modern machines find in the lake?
Why do people still visit the lake every year?
options: They enjoy the mystery and hope to see something.

questions.stem: What does Mia think might happen one day?
options: Someone may get a clear photo.

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 A Tip for Taking Notes
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is a useful tip for when you listen to a report about a discovery.
Speakers often give important numbers, such as dates, sizes and distances.
These numbers can be easy to miss if you are not ready for them.
So keep a pen in your hand and write each number down at once.
Good notes will help you remember the facts long after the talk ends.
exercises.translation_cn: 这是一个在听有关发现的报告时很有用的小贴士:讲话者常会给出重要数字,如日期、大小和距离;如果没准备好,这些数字很容易被漏掉;所以手里拿支笔,把每个数字立刻记下来;好的笔记能帮你在讲话结束很久后仍记住这些事实。

questions.stem: When is this tip useful?
options: When listening to a report about a discovery.
